findings.summary: Two sections have their heading stranded at the end of one page while the body lands on the next, and in one case the receiving page's title does not cover the content it opens with.
findings.evidence: Page 1's last block is the heading "Parse Flags With getopts" (the `while getopts` code is page 2's first block); page 2's last block is the heading "Tracing Leaks Secrets Too" while page 3 is titled "Portability, Safety Core & Shipping Tests" and opens with the `set +x` / `curl -H "Auth: $TOK"` block.
findings.fix: Move each trailing heading onto the page that carries its body, and either move the tracing/secrets block back onto page 2 or rename page 3 to name it (e.g. "Tracing, Portability & Shipping Tests").

findings.summary: The claim that sourcing the file only defines it is contradicted by the very code block above it, which calls `main` unconditionally.
findings.evidence: Bullet: "Sourcing the file ==defines== but does not run" — but the skeleton shows `main "$@"   # nothing below this` with no source guard, so `source ./script.sh` does run main.
findings.fix: Show the guard in the skeleton code: `[[ ${BASH_SOURCE[0]} == "$0" ]] && main "$@"`, or drop the sourcing bullet and keep the claim to "a truncated download cannot half-execute".

findings.summary: `die()` is defined twice on the same page with different bodies and no statement that the second replaces the first.
findings.evidence: "The die Helper": `die() { echo "$*" >&2; exit 2; }`, then three blocks later "Logs To stderr, Data To stdout": `die() { log "error: $*"; exit 2; }`.
findings.fix: Teach `log()` first, then define `die()` once on top of it (`die() { log "error: $*"; exit 1; }`), and delete the `echo`-based version — the handbook's own footgun rule says `printf '%s\n'` over `echo` for untrusted values.

findings.summary: `die()` hardcodes `exit 2` for a missing file, before exit-code meanings are taught on page 2, and it conflicts with the table when they are.
findings.evidence: Page 1: `die() { echo "$*" >&2; exit 2; }` used as `[[ -f $cfg ]] || die "no $cfg"`. Page 2 table: ["`2`","usage error","bad flag, missing arg"].
findings.fix: Make `die()` exit 1 (general error) and use an explicit `usage >&2; exit 2` in the bad-flag branch only; or move the "Exit Codes That Mean Something" table ahead of "The die Helper" so the codes are defined before they are used.

findings.summary: The `usage()` helper is defined to write to stderr, contradicting the page-2 rule it is later invoked under.
findings.evidence: Page 1: `usage() { echo "$USAGE" >&2; }`. Page 2: "`-h` always supported — usage to **stdout**" with `h) usage; exit 0 ;;` and `*) usage >&2; exit 2 ;;` (a redirect that is a no-op if usage already writes to stderr).
findings.fix: Define `usage() { printf '%s\n' "$USAGE"; }` writing to stdout, so `-h` prints to stdout and the error branch's `usage >&2` is what redirects it.

findings.summary: The section heading "Tracing Leaks Secrets Too" renders with no body content beneath it, leaving a large empty gap in the left column.
findings.evidence: Page 2 left column: heading "→ Tracing Leaks Secrets Too" is followed by roughly 300px of blank space before the next heading ("Exit Codes That Mean Something"); its code block ("set +x / curl -H "Auth: $TOK" "$url" / set -x") appears at the top of page 3 with no heading.
findings.fix: Keep the "Tracing Leaks Secrets Too" heading with its code block — move the heading onto page 3 above that block (or pull the block up to page 2) so heading and content stay on the same page.
Run the fit pass — it adds material from the book without removing anything.

findings.summary: The caption's first sentence is a series label rather than a hook, pushing the actual hook past Instagram's feed truncation point.
findings.evidence: "Part 2 of BASH SCRIPT SAFETY. `cd /nonexistent; rm -rf *` — two commands, one deleted working directory, zero error messages." — the first sentence carries no hook, and the hook sentence ends at ~126 characters, past the ~125-character preview cutoff.
findings.fix: Lead with the hook and move the series label after it: "`cd /nonexistent; rm -rf *` — two commands, one deleted working directory, zero error messages. Part 2 of BASH SCRIPT SAFETY. Bash's default is to keep going no matter what, ..."

findings.summary: The heading "Parse Flags With getopts" is orphaned at the bottom of page 1 with its content on page 2.
findings.evidence: Page 1 right column ends with "→ Parse Flags With getopts" and nothing under it; page 2 opens with the unlabelled block "while getopts ":ho:" f; do ... esac; done".
findings.fix: Move the "Parse Flags With getopts" heading to page 2 so it sits directly above the getopts code block.

findings.summary: `$USAGE` is referenced in the helper but never defined or shown anywhere in the part.
findings.evidence: `usage() { echo "$USAGE" >&2; }` — no block sets `USAGE`, while `VERSION` is shown as `readonly VERSION=1.4.0`.
findings.fix: Show the assignment in the same code block, e.g. a quoted here-doc: `read -r -d '' USAGE <<'EOF' ... EOF` or put the here-doc inside `usage()` directly.

findings.summary: A quoting rule is filed inside the "Test Before Production" checklist, where it does not belong.
findings.evidence: Under "Test Before Production": "`rm -- \"$f\"` so a leading dash isn't a flag" — the other four items are bats-core, shfmt, dry-run, and running the failure path.
findings.fix: Move that bullet up beside the safety-core / quoting bullets and, if a fifth test item is wanted, replace it with "shellcheck + shfmt run in CI, not just locally".
